articles.detail: 5 cycles, 4 completed, avg 9 published/cycle (42 yesterday); 0 quarantined

experiment: Skipped. No experiments are active and there is no pause gate. Today is the second clean day after the 09-25/26 pipeline changes, and every target except multi-source was met. The plan from 09-27 stands: revisit on 2026-09-30 with three clean days.
weakestArea: Multi-source share is 29% against a 30% target (18 of 58 articles), down from 43% yesterday. It is one article short, and the multi-source count was 18 on both days, so the drop comes from 17 more articles, almost all single-source, not from fewer corroborated stories. If it stays under 30% through 09-30, look at the selector's multi-source enforcement before touching feed parameters. The 2026-05-09 floor-3 experiment was reverted, so do not repeat it.
watching: Iran: Trump is weighing sanctions relief through Qatari mediators while Marines were hurt in a Hormuz strike and oil spiked on Iran's rejection. The relief story is state-or-advocacy-only sourced so far.
Nigeria: the AAC is suing Tinubu over his absence and a power transfer to Shettima, while the Senate panel halted the Discos sale.
France: the RN won a Senate group, and Bardella is fighting the Mediapart antisemitism reporting.
Venezuela: rallies for Machado, one of three Latin American stories alongside El Salvador's gang war and Lula's Amazon record.
Russia: Putin's decree raises the army ceiling to 2.44 million, and there are reports of a mystery missile aiding Russia.
Pakistan: TTAP joins PTI's October 4 march, and the Hangor missile test.
coverageGaps: Oceania has one story (Australia summoning Altman and Amodei), and nothing is regional to the Pacific.
Freshness was measured on only 6 of 59 articles, so the median is not representative.
India still takes a large share of Asia (Ujjain, Uttar Pradesh, Sensex, Tata Trusts). East and Southeast Asia coverage improved, with Korea, Malaysia and Laos/Thailand.
One of five cycles did not complete, and the average cycle took 1242s, up from 963s.
context: Science recovered to 7 (from 3) across four dedicated outlets (Nature Communications, Phys.org, Carbon Brief, Ars Technica), which argues against changing the science floor. US datelines held at 21% and Latin America rose to 7%, so the US cap and pool widening met both geography targets for a second day. There were no same-event duplicates and nothing was quarantined.
